rules.statement: Don't make a change pass by skipping, deleting or weakening an existing test or its assertions; fix the code under test instead.
rules.why: A skipped or weakened test is a shortcut that hides the defect it was meant to catch, even though the checks then pass.
rules.check: Look in the diff for tests that were removed, marked skipped, or had assertions loosened or deleted without the behavior they cover being removed.

rules.statement: Don't swallow exceptions: a catch block must handle, translate, log or rethrow the error, not discard it silently.
rules.why: The review treats swallowed errors as a shortcut that hides failures instead of handling them.
rules.check: Look for empty catch blocks, or catch blocks that ignore the exception and continue, without a comment explaining why ignoring it is correct.

rules.statement: Don't leave TODO comments or hard-coded placeholder values in place of the behavior the change was supposed to implement.
rules.why: Leftover TODOs and hard-coded values are shortcuts that make the checks pass while the real behavior is still missing.
rules.check: Search added lines for TODO/FIXME/HACK markers and for literal values that stand in for configuration or computed results.

rules.statement: When reviewing work done from a plan, flag any deviation from the step's text as at least should-fix, even when its checks pass. Deviations include touching files the step doesn't list, changing an interface, or creating something the step says already exists.
rules.why: A deviation means the executor improvised instead of escalating.
rules.check: Compare each changed file and interface in the diff against the Files and Change text of the plan step it belongs to.
